item.title: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raises $8M to run AI on satellites
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.

item.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, called its most powerful model yet
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Google has released its latest Gemini model, marketing it as a workhorse for coding and cybersecurity work.

item.title: The Pentagon taps Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to help decide what the military should do next
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth just launched a 120-day study on the future of warfare, led by Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich, and while it makes sense given their ties to the administration, critics could point out that Musk's and Luckey's companies already sell the kinds of technology the study is likely to recommend.

item.title: Valor, Atreides, and Sequoia back AI startup Flow Engineering at $750M valuation
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Flow Engineering, which is bringing AI agents to hardware design, also landed Roelof Botha as an angel investor and board member.

item.title: Factory CEO just accused his VC board adviser of spying for Cognition
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: VC Chris Degnan and former board adviser to Factory AI has taken a job as chief revenue officer for competitor Cognition -- and everyone is arguing on X about it.

item.title: Is Neko Health’s body scan worth it? Spotify billionaire’s startup has come to America
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo
item.description: Spotify founder Daniel Ek’s Neko Health raised $700 million to build a business around scanning your body, but it’s not the only company centering its roadmap around a new kind of preventative healthcare. Midjourney is building its own body scanner, while Function Health has also raised significant capital to build out its preventative-health platform. Why are investors betting so big on this category? On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, […]

item.title: Hackers stole millions of US military personnel records during months-long data breach
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The Department of Defense notified millions of current and former U.S. military personnel that their personal information had been stolen in a months-long breach.

item.title: DoorDash’s drone strategy started on the ground
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: DoorDash unveiled the six-propeller aircraft that will be used in its new drone delivery business at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event.

item.title: BMW built the same car for gas and electric. The EV is $4,400 cheaper.
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: The new BMW 3 Series shows just how quickly EVs have caught up to fossil fuel vehicles on pricing.

item.title: OpenAI’s Jev clone could help the frontier lab stop its swarming agents
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: OpenAI's "Decisions API" is a Jev clone that confirms the importance of fast, cheap intelligence.

item.title: AI voice startup ElevenLabs doubles valuation to $22B
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: The $300 million employee tender was co-led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price.

item.title: Reddit is killing RSS feeds and ending public API access because of AI bots
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Reddit is ending support for RSS feeds, as the company continues tightening access to its trove of user-generated content.

item.title: The ugly economics of consumer AI
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: There’s a reason frontier labs have gotten gun-shy about consumer AI — and it’s not because the tech isn’t good enough.

item.title: Meta disputes claim that Muse read a user’s private messages without permission
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Meta says its Muse AI agent cannot access a user’s Messages without explicit permission, disputing a journalist’s account that the agent read his private messages while the required Mac setting was turned off.

item.title: DoorDash launches an AI agent you can text to order food
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: By launching an AI agent for food ordering, DoorDash is looking to gain an edge over rivals Uber Eats and Grubhub.

item.title: Destro AI’s secret sauce is getting robots and humans on the same page
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: "One of the biggest reasons we are winning against robotics companies is because we are not a robotics company."

item.title: Instinct’s new product recommendations are giving some users the ick
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Instinct is rolling out human-curated product and travel recommendations, but some users aren’t happy about getting suggestions they never asked for.

item.title: FedEx orders 2,000 electric trucks from Harbinger in $300M deal
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The order -- Harbinger's biggest ever -- comes as the startup is reportedly considering an IPO.

item.title: Pledge signed by President Trump and top AI leaders misspells the United States
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: On Tuesday, President Donald Trump and top AI leaders announced a signed pledge called a “Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities” — a voluntary promise to implement more controls and safety measures as the rapid development of artificial intelligence continues. But there seems to be a catch.

item.title: Google launches Fitbit Air in India, though its high price might deter the masses
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Fitbit Air costs around $146 in India, roughly $47 more than its U.S. pricing.
